Lemma
[equality in the energy comparison]

↗ lem:dc-ch9-2-3-geodesic-equality ↗ lem:dc-ch9-2-2-schwarz ↗ def:dc-ch9-2-2-energy

1. ch9:2.3In the situation of section 1, if moreover $E(\gamma )=E(c)$, then (a) the speed $|dc/dt|$ is (almost everywhere) constant, i.e. the parameter of $c$ is proportional to arc length; and (b) $L(\gamma )=L(c)$, i.e. $c$ is minimizing too.

Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch9-2-3-geodesic-equality ↗ lem:dc-ch9-2-2-schwarz \sketch Under $E(\gamma )=E(c)$ every inequality in the chain $(b-a)E(\gamma )=L(\gamma )^2\le L(c)^2\le (b-a)E(c)$ of section 1 collapses to an equality. From $L(c)^2=(b-a)E(c)$ and the equality case of section 1, the speed of $c$ is a.e. constant, which is (a); from $L(\gamma )^2=L(c)^2$ and non-negativity of both lengths, $L(\gamma )=L(c)$, which is (b).

□
